arxiv-2012-00683.title: Prospect for application of mathematical models in combination cancer treatments ∗ Corresponding author: Henry A. Adeola , Email address: henry.adeola@uct.ac.za
arxiv-2012-00683.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by . The long-term efficacy of targeted therapeutics for cancer treatment can be significantly limited by the type of therapy and development of drug resistance, inter alia. Experimental studies indicate that the factors enhancing acquisition of drug resistance in cancer cells include cell heterogeneity, drug target alteration, drug inactivation, DNA damage repair, drug efflux, cell death inhibition, as well as microenvironmental adaptations to targeted therapy, among others.

arxiv-2102-00447.title: Social Mobility in India
arxiv-2102-00447.creator: A. Singh, Department of Economics, Finance, Pilani Campus, India, A. Forcina, Dipartimento di Economia, Perugia, Italy, K. Muniyoor, Department of Economics, Finance, Pilani Campus, India
arxiv-2102-00447.description: Abstract Rapid rise in income inequality in India is a serious concern. While the emphasis is on inclusive growth, it seems difficult to tackle the problem without looking at the intricacies of the problem. Social mobility is one such important tool which helps in reaching the cause of the problem and focuses on bringing long term equality in the country.

arxiv-2206-03944.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Digital Interventions: Pre-implementation Guidelines
arxiv-2206-03944.creator: Anna L. Trella, Kelly W. Zhang, Inbal Nahum-Shani, Vivek Shetty, Finale Doshi-Velez, Susan A. Murphy
arxiv-2206-03944.description: Abstract Online reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are increasingly used to personalize digital interventions in the fields of mobile health and online education. Common challenges in designing and testing an RL algorithm in these settings include ensuring the RL algorithm can learn and run stably under real-time constraints, and accounting for the complexity of the environment, e.g.

arxiv-2210-16095.title: Sequential hypothesis testing for Axion Haloscopes
arxiv-2210-16095.creator: Andrea Gallo Rosso, Sara Algeri, Jan Conrad
arxiv-2210-16095.description: Abstract The goal of this paper is to introduce a novel likelihood-based inferential framework for axion haloscopes which is valid under the commonly applied “rescanning” protocol. The proposed method enjoys short data acquisition times and a simple tuning of the detector configuration. Local statistical significance and power are computed analytically, avoiding the need of burdensome simulations.

arxiv-2302-00768.title: Leveraging Task Dependency and Contrastive Learning for Case Outcome Classification on European Court of Human Rights Cases
arxiv-2302-00768.creator: Santosh T.Y.S.S, Marcel Perez San Blas, Phillip Kemper, Matthias Grabmair
arxiv-2302-00768.description: Abstract We report on an experiment in case outcome classification on European Court of Human Rights cases where our model first learns to identify the convention articles allegedly violated by the state from case facts descriptions, and subsequently uses that information to classify whether the court finds a violation of those articles.

arxiv-2309-00200.title: Observations of a black hole X-ray binary indicate formation of a magnetically arrested disk
arxiv-2309-00200.creator: Bei You, Xinwu Cao, Zhen Yan, Jean-Marie Hameury, Bozena Czerny, Yue Wu, Tianyu Xia, Marek Sikora, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Pu Du, Piotr T. Zycki

arxiv-2402-10447.title: Incremental Sequence Labeling: A Tale of Two Shifts Thanks: *Corresponding author
arxiv-2402-10447.creator: Shengjie Qiu, Junhao Zheng, Zhen Liu, Yicheng Luo, Qianli Ma*
arxiv-2402-10447.description: Abstract The incremental sequence labeling task involves continuously learning new classes over time while retaining knowledge of the previous ones. Our investigation identifies two significant semantic shifts: E2O (where the model mislabels an old entity as a non-entity) and O2E (where the model labels a non-entity or old entity as a new entity).

arxiv-2412-02177.title: Anatomically-Grounded Fact Checking of Automated Chest X-ray Reports
arxiv-2412-02177.creator: R. Mahmood, D. M. Reyes, G. Wang, P. Yan, P. Kaviani, M. Kalra, K.C.L. Wong, N. D’Souza, L. Shi, J. Wu, T. Syeda-Mahmood
arxiv-2412-02177.description: Abstract With the emergence of large-scale vision-language models, realistic radiology reports may be generated using only medical images as input guided by simple prompts. However, their practical utility has been limited due to the factual errors in their description of findings.

arxiv-2504-13319.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fridolin Melong † and Raimar Wulkenhaar ‡. We investigate the ℛ ⁡ ( p , q ) \mathcal{R}(p,q) -super n n -bracket and study their properties such that the generalized super Jacobi identity (GJSI). arxiv-2505-06312.title: Responsibility Gap in Collective Decision Making
arxiv-2505-06312.creator: Pavel Naumov, Jia Tao
arxiv-2505-06312.description: Abstract The responsibility gap is a set of outcomes of a collective decision-making mechanism in which no single agent is individually responsible. In general, when designing a decision-making process, it is desirable to minimise the gap. The paper proposes a concept of an elected dictatorship.

arxiv-2505-16739.title: Asymptotics of the partition function of the perturbed Gross-Witten-Wadia unitary matrix model
arxiv-2505-16739.creator: Yu Chen, Shuai-Xia Xu, Yu-Qiu Zhao
arxiv-2505-16739.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yu Chen, Shuai-Xia Xu, Yu-Qiu Zhao. We consider the asymptotics of the partition function of the extended Gross-Witten-Wadia unitary matrix model by introducing an extra logarithmic term in the potential. The partition function can be written as a Toeplitz determinant with entries expressed in terms of the modified Bessel functions of the first kind and furnishes a τ \tau -function sequence of the Painlevé III ′ equation.

arxiv-2507-15156.title: Constraint-aware Learning of Probabilistic Sequential Models for Multi-Label Classification
arxiv-2507-15156.creator: Mykhailo Buleshnyi, Anna Polova, Zsolt Zombori, Michael Benedikt
arxiv-2507-15156.description: Abstract . We investigate multi-label classification involving large sets of labels, where the output labels may be known to satisfy some logical constraints. We look at an architecture in which classifiers for individual labels are fed into an expressive sequential model, which produces a joint distribution.

arxiv-2512-02125.title: A value-added catalogue of neural network-based europium abundances for GALAH DR4 2026 A value-added catalogue of neural network-based europium abundances for GALAH DR4 – 17
arxiv-2512-02125.creator: Sarah G. Kane, Zofia Kaczmarek, Andrew Garner, Sven Buder, Stephanie Monty, and Elana Kane
arxiv-2512-02125.description: Abstract The rapid neutron-capture ( r r -process) element europium (Eu) is a valuable tracer of neutron star mergers and other rare nucleosynthetic events. The stellar spectroscopic survey GALAH’s unique wavelength range and setup include the Eu absorption feature at ∼ 6645 \sim 6645 Å for almost a million stars in the most recent Data Release 4 (DR4).

arxiv-2602-02648.title: Quantum criticality at strong randomness: a lesson from anomaly
arxiv-2602-02648.creator: Yasamin Panahi, Subhayan Sahu, Naren Manjunath, Chong Wang (王翀)
arxiv-2602-02648.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yasamin Panahi, Subhayan Sahu, Naren Manjunath, Chong Wang (王翀). Quantum criticality in the presence of strong quenched randomness remains a challenging topic in modern condensed matter theory. We show that the topology and anomaly associated with average symmetry can be used to predict certain nontrivial universal properties. Our focus is on systems subject to average Lieb–Schultz–Mattis constraints, where lattice translation symmetry is preserved only on average, while on-site symmetries remain exact.

pmc-10753706.title: Nanomedicine-Based Drug-Targeting in Breast Cancer: Pharmacokinetics, Clinical Progress, and Challenges
pmc-10753706.creator: Mahfoozur Rahman, Obaid Afzal, Shehla Nasar Mir
pmc-10753706.description: Breast cancer (BC) is a malignant neoplasm that begins in the breast tissue. After skin cancer, BC is the second most common type of cancer in women. At the end of 2040, the number of newly diagnosed BC cases is projected to increase by over 40%, reaching approximately 3 million worldwide annually.

pmc-11328381.title: Longitudinal assessment of the impact of COVID-19 infection on mask-wearing behaviors
pmc-11328381.creator: Danielle Pham, Angel Lomeli, Nicole H Goldhaber, Holly D Valentine, Rob Knight, Christopher A Longhurst, Louise C Laurent, Marni B Jacobs
pmc-11328381.description: BackgroundWearing a mask was a crucial component in slowing the COVID-19 pandemic. However, little is known about the intersectionality between mask usage, risk perception, and infection. The purpose of this study was to investigate whether risk perceptions and masking behaviors are associated with contracting SARS-CoV-2 and how contracting SARS-CoV-2 subsequently changes masking behaviors in specific situations.

pmc-11460111.title: Predictors of genital self–image in Iranian women: a cross–sectional study
pmc-11460111.creator: Mina Malary, Zeinab Hamzehgardeshi, Afsaneh Keramat, Masoud Yunesian, Maryam Farjamfar
pmc-11460111.description: Background and AimSeveral factors influence women’s perception of their genitalia. Understanding the elements associated with genital self‑image (GSI) can significantly contribute to enhancing women’s sexual experiences. Therefore, the present study aimed to identify the predictors of GSI in Iranian women.

pmc-11644083.title: Dynamic Thermo-Mechanical Properties of Carbon Nanotube Resin Composite Films
pmc-11644083.creator: Ying Wang, Zhouyi Li, Yan Liu, Penghao Pei
pmc-11644083.description: In this paper, we prepared carbon nanotube (CNT) epoxy composite films and conducted tensile experiments at various temperatures (−40 °C, −10 °C, 20 °C, and 50 °C) and frequencies (1 Hz, 10 Hz, and 20 Hz) using Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA).

pmc-12360001.title: A mixed-method exploratory assessment of provider-based stigma of opioid use disorder (OUD) and support for medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) in carceral settings
pmc-12360001.creator: Katherine J McLean, Nathan E Kruis, Eric Weintraub, Heather Fitzsimons, Christopher Welsh, Natalie Spicyn, Brook Kearley, William Altekruse, Nicholas Rowland, Annabelle Belcher
pmc-12360001.description: BackgroundIn 2019, the state of Maryland passed legislation requiring local detention centers to offer medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) to all incarcerated individuals who met criteria for opioid use disorder (OUD). Four years later, many facilities remain out of compliance. Beyond issues of staffing, funding, and technical support, stigma may represent a barrier to MOUD implementation.

pmc-12527594.title: A Prospective Observational Study of Intraoperative Regional Cerebral Desaturation and Negative Postoperative Behavioural Changes After Non‐Cardiac Paediatric Surgery
pmc-12527594.creator: Martin Kälvesten, Ali‐Reza Modiri, Rececka Jonshult, Robert Frithiof, Peter Frykholm
pmc-12527594.description: BackgroundNegative postoperative behaviour changes (NPOBC) are known to occur after general anaesthesia in children. A significantly increased risk of NPOBC has been reported in children who exhibited a reduction in cerebral regional oxygen saturation (crSO2) of as little as 5% below baseline levels.

pmc-13156003.title: Analysis of Morphological High-Risk Factors for Retrograde Type A Aortic Dissection
pmc-13156003.creator: Chaozhong Long, Jinhai Xia, Chaoen Luo, Jinzhou Cai, Asfandyar Khan, Yaoguang Feng, Zhengwen Lei
pmc-13156003.description: Background:The mechanism involved in retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD) remains unclear, while research through morphological studies is limited. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the aortic geometric features between RTAD and type B aortic dissection (TBAD) and to identify specific anatomical predictors of RTAD.

pmc-13262438.title: The prognostic value of the Oocyte Maturation Index (OMI) on pregnancy outcomes in POSEIDON group 3 and 4 patients: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13262438.creator: Yakup Bayram, Hamza Yildiz, Gorkem Ulger, Huseyin Durukan, Devrim Tok, Faik Gurkan Yazici
pmc-13262438.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis study aims to evaluate the prognostic value of the Oocyte Maturation Index (OMI) on fertilization, embryo development, and pregnancy outcomes in young (POSEIDON Group 3) and older (POSEIDON Group 4) patients with diminished ovarian reserve.MethodsA total of 662 patients treated at the Assisted Reproductive Techniques Unit of Mersin University Faculty of Medicine between 2016 and 2024 (Group 3: n=245; Group 4: n=417) were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-13276835.title: Toward Precision Electrochemical Sensing of CFTR Function in Cystic Fibrosis Models
pmc-13276835.creator: Antonella Miglione, Giovanna Blaconà, Sima Singh, Stefania Lo Cicero, Andrea Fuso, Giuseppe Cimino, Adriana Eramo, Umberto Malapelle, Marco Lucarelli, Stefano Cinti
pmc-13276835.description: The assessment of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) activity is essential to both diagnose and evaluate the efficacy of treatments in cystic fibrosis (CF). In particular, the prompt evaluation of genotype-specific responses to CFTR modulators might lead to more precise therapeutic approaches.

pmc-13575611.title: Effects of an Ultrasound‑Guided Femoral, Sciatic, and Genitofemoral Nerve Block with Ropivacaine on EC50 and EC95 for High Saphenous Vein Ligation
pmc-13575611.creator: Hui Wang, Jiangtao Chang, Yufei Li, Lina Chen, Changjun Chen, Qiuru Wang, Xiaojun Gao, Fan Yang, Songsong Chen, Yuelan Wang, Jianbo Wu, Guanghan Wu
pmc-13575611.description: PurposeTo determine the effective concentrations (EC50 and EC95) of ropivacaine for an ultrasound-guided triple nerve block (femoral(FNB), suprapopliteal sciatic(SPSB), and genitofemoral nerve femoral branch(GFNfB)) in patients undergoing high saphenous vein ligation and stripping.MethodsThirty-six patients scheduled for elective unilateral high saphenous vein ligation and stripping were enrolled. Nerve blocks were performed under ultrasound guidance.

pmc-13651748.creator: Mattison P. Stojcic, Makenzie A. Manning, Miguel Galicchio, Manfred Hönig, Despina Moshous, Sven Kracker, Felipe Suarez, Ruben Martinez-Barricarte, Aidé Tamara Staines-Boone, Yuridia Salazar Gálvez, Edgar-Domingo Cordero-Chura, Estefany-Graciela Mamani-Velasquez

pmc-13680610.title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
pmc-13680610.creator: Viacheslav Korolev, Thomas Lettau, Vipin Krishna, Alexander Croy, Martin Thümmler, Michael Zürch, Christian Spielmann, Maria Wächtler, Ulf Peschel, Stefanie Gräfe, Giancarlo Soavi, Daniil Kartashov
pmc-13680610.description: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved.

uslaw-usc-t21-s2011.title: 21 U.S.C. § 2011 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t21-s2011.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s2011.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 25 (Miscellaneous Anti-Drug Abuse Provisions); Subchapter II (National Methamphetamine Information Clearinghouse). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this subchapter— (1) the term “Council” means the National Methamphetamine Advisory Council established under section 2012(b)(1) of this title; (2) the term “drug endangered children” means children whose physical, mental, or emotional health are at risk.
